clusters.label: NLP Definitions
clusters.rationale: These candidates provide core definitions of Natural Language Processing, describing it as an AI subfield that enables machines to understand human language, with mention of foundational fields or statistical nature. They are at the same definitional level and can be tested with a unified 'Define NLP' question.

clusters.label: NLP Applications
clusters.rationale: Both candidates list and describe practical applications of NLP, from everyday tools like autocorrect to broader uses like machine translation and sentiment analysis. They cover the same teachable idea of what NLP can do.

clusters.label: NLP Challenges
clusters.rationale: These candidates discuss difficulties in NLP, such as segmentation, ambiguity, and the variability of natural language. They address the same fundamental question: what makes NLP challenging?

clusters.label: Word Normalization
clusters.rationale: This candidate specifically covers stemming and lemmatization, distinct preprocessing techniques. No other candidate shares this precise focus.

clusters.label: Linguistic Annotation
clusters.rationale: This candidate explains POS tagging and Named Entity Recognition, specific annotation tasks in NLP. It stands alone as no other candidate covers the same techniques.

clusters.label: Machine Learning in NLP
clusters.rationale: This candidate describes the role of machine learning in NLP, using Naive Bayes as an example. It is a standalone concept about the ML pipeline component.

clusters.label: NLP Definition and Suitability Criteria
clusters.rationale: This candidate defines NLP and adds specific criteria for when NLP is suitable (understanding communication, precision, large data volumes). This combined idea is unique among the candidates.

clusters.label: Text Vectorization for Machine Learning
clusters.rationale: This candidate explains why text must be converted to numerical representations for ML algorithms, an implementation-level concept not duplicated in other candidates.

clusters.label: Artificial Neural Network
clusters.rationale: This candidate defines artificial neural networks, a general AI concept. It does not share the same teachable idea with the other NLP-focused candidates.

clusters.label: Text Normalization/Cleaning
clusters.rationale: Both candidates describe the same essential preprocessing steps—lowercasing, removing punctuation and special characters and often stop words—to clean and normalize raw text before further processing. They share the same teachable idea of basic text cleaning for NLP.

clusters.label: Text Preprocessing: Segmentation, Tokenization, and Stop Words
clusters.rationale: Broader candidate that includes sentence segmentation in addition to tokenization and stop words, so kept separate from narrower tokenization-only candidates.

clusters.label: Text Preprocessing: Tokenization and Stopword Removal
clusters.rationale: Combines tokenization with stopword removal in a single package; no other candidate covers exactly this combination at the same level.

clusters.label: Tokenization with NLTK
clusters.rationale: Focuses specifically on NLTK tokenization and its advantages with contractions; tool-specific behavior not matched by general tokenization candidates.

clusters.label: Handling Portuguese text encoding (ISO 8859-1)
clusters.rationale: Unique candidate about encoding detection and decoding for Portuguese text files; no other candidate covers text encoding.

clusters.label: Stop Words Removal
clusters.rationale: Focused only on identifying and removing stop words using pre-defined lists; distinct from candidates that bundle stop words with tokenization.

clusters.label: Word-level Tokenization
clusters.rationale: General word tokenization without tool-specific details; kept separate from NLTK-specific tokenization.

clusters.label: Vocabulary Construction and Out-of-Vocabulary Handling
clusters.rationale: Distinct concept of building a frequency-filtered vocabulary and strategies for unknown words; no other candidate covers vocabulary construction.

clusters.label: Alternation and Grouping: | and ()
clusters.rationale: Covers logical OR and subexpression grouping; unique among the candidates.

clusters.label: Escaping Metacharacters: \
clusters.rationale: Covers treating metacharacters as literals; distinct from other concepts.

clusters.label: Shorthand Character Classes: \d, \w, \s
